messages.content: Registration finally answered. Check-in closes at 10:00 a.m. Monday, and the workshop is at Music City Center. I do not want to gamble on the 6:05 Monday flight, so use the Sunday option. Now compare a couple of downtown hotels, make sure Tuesday's 5:15 return is realistic after the 2:00 finish, and get this booked.

The Sunday flight is the sound choice. I still see the nonstop leaving ORD at 6:20 p.m. and arriving BNA at 7:55 p.m.; the Tuesday nonstop leaves BNA at 5:15 p.m. and arrives ORD at 7:05 p.m. The round-trip fare is now $351.

For two nights downtown, the strongest practical options near Music City Center are Embassy Suites by Hilton Nashville Downtown and Hampton Inn & Suites Nashville-Downtown. I’ll verify walking distance, complete totals, and cancellation terms before recommending one. Are you traveling alone, and will you have only a carry-on or a checked bag?
Alone. One carry-on, no checked bag. I will leave it with the hotel Tuesday morning and pick it up after the workshop.

That makes the Tuesday return feasible. Music City Center to either hotel is only a short walk, so you can retrieve the bag quickly. After a 2:00 p.m. finish, a reasonable sequence is to collect the carry-on by about 2:20, request a rideshare, and reach BNA around 2:50 to 3:10 in normal traffic. That leaves more than two hours before departure.

The two verified hotel options are:

Embassy Suites Nashville Downtown: about a four-minute walk to Music City Center. One king room for Sunday and Monday nights is $612.44 total, including taxes and mandatory fees. Breakfast is included. Cancellation is free until 11:59 p.m. local time on Thursday, October 31; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax.

Hampton Inn & Suites Nashville-Downtown: about a five-minute walk. One king room is $548.16 total, including taxes and mandatory fees. Breakfast is included. Cancellation is free until 6:00 p.m. local time on Friday, November 1; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax.

The Hampton is the better value and is equally workable for the workshop and airport departure.
Is there any reason to pay the extra $64 for Embassy Suites?

The main differences are space and convenience inside the room: Embassy Suites provides a separate living area, and its evening reception is included. It is also roughly one minute closer on foot, which is immaterial here. Both properties include breakfast, both can hold your carry-on after checkout, and neither offers an airport shuttle. For a two-night solo work stay, those benefits do not justify the additional $64.28 unless you need the separate room for meetings.
I don't. Before booking, check the flight schedule one more time and tell me whether the 5:15 flight is the first return you would actually recommend. I don't want a connection.

I rechecked nonstop Tuesday returns from BNA to ORD after the workshop. There is a 3:35 p.m. departure, but it is not realistic: you would need to leave the venue before the 2:00 p.m. finish and would have almost no margin to retrieve your bag. The 5:15 p.m. nonstop is the first return I would recommend. The next nonstop leaves at 7:10 p.m. and arrives at 8:58 p.m.; it adds margin but also nearly two hours of waiting.

The 5:15 flight remains available at the quoted itinerary total of $351 and gives adequate time if the workshop ends on schedule.
What if the closing discussion runs fifteen or twenty minutes late?

It still works. If you leave Music City Center at 2:20, walk to the Hampton, and have your carry-on by 2:35, a typical rideshare would put you at BNA around 3:05 to 3:25. Even allowing another 15 minutes for traffic, you would arrive about 95 minutes before the 5:15 departure.

The schedule becomes uncomfortable if the workshop runs past roughly 2:45 or if there is a significant traffic incident. The 7:10 flight removes that concern, but for the stated 2:00 finish with a possible 20-minute overrun, 5:15 is a practical choice.
Keep 5:15. Does that $351 include a normal economy seat and the carry-on? I do not want a restrictive fare that makes me pay to choose a seat.

Yes. The $351 itinerary is standard economy, not basic economy. It includes one carry-on and advance selection of a standard seat at no additional charge. Changes are permitted without a change fee, although any fare difference would apply. The ticket is nonrefundable to the original payment method; if canceled before departure, its value is retained as an airline credit under the fare rules.
Good. Give me the complete Sunday and Tuesday schedule with the hotel total once more. Then book the flight and Hampton if nothing changed.

Final itinerary before purchase:

Sunday, November 3: nonstop ORD-BNA, departing 6:20 p.m. and arriving 7:55 p.m.
Tuesday, November 5: nonstop BNA-ORD, departing 5:15 p.m. and arriving 7:05 p.m.
Standard economy round trip for Marcus Lee: $351.00, including one carry-on and standard seat selection.

Hampton Inn & Suites Nashville-Downtown, November 3-5: one king room for two nights, $548.16 total including taxes and mandatory fees. Breakfast is included. Free cancellation runs through 6:00 p.m. Nashville time on Friday, November 1; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. The hotel has confirmed that it will hold your carry-on after Tuesday checkout.

The combined total is $899.16. I’m proceeding with both reservations.
Proceed.

The flight and hotel are confirmed.

Flight confirmation: N4V7QC. The charged round-trip total is $351.00. You are booked in standard economy on the Sunday 6:20 p.m. ORD-BNA nonstop, arriving 7:55 p.m., and the Tuesday 5:15 p.m. BNA-ORD nonstop, arriving 7:05 p.m. One carry-on is included. Standard seats can be selected without an added charge.

Hotel confirmation: HND-730418. The Hampton Inn & Suites Nashville-Downtown is booked for November 3-5 in one king room for Marcus Lee. The complete two-night total is $548.16 including taxes and mandatory fees, with breakfast included. Cancellation is free through 6:00 p.m. Nashville time on November 1; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax.
Assign seats if there are decent ones, and confirm the ground plan. I need the Tuesday timing stated clearly because that is the tight part.
Available standard seats include 14A and 14C outbound, and 12A and 13D on the return. All are regular economy seats. Would you like the window seats, 14A Sunday and 12A Tuesday, or the aisle seats?
Take the windows.

Seats are assigned: 14A on the Sunday outbound and 12A on the Tuesday return. There was no additional charge.

Sunday ground plan: after the 7:55 p.m. arrival, use rideshare from BNA to the Hampton Inn & Suites Nashville-Downtown. Allow about 15-25 minutes for the drive in normal evening traffic, plus pickup time.

Monday: the hotel is about a five-minute walk from Music City Center, so leaving by 9:35 a.m. gives enough time to arrive before the 10:00 a.m. check-in cutoff.

Tuesday: check out in the morning and leave the carry-on with the front desk. When the workshop ends at 2:00 p.m., walk back to the hotel and aim to have the bag in hand by 2:20. Request a rideshare immediately and target departure from the hotel no later than 2:30. Expected arrival at BNA is approximately 2:50-3:10; even with a 20-minute workshop overrun, you should reach the airport around 3:10-3:30. That preserves at least 105 minutes before the 5:15 p.m. flight. If the session runs beyond 2:40, leave promptly and monitor the drive time before retrieving the bag.

Nashville is fully confirmed under flight code N4V7QC and hotel code HND-730418, with a combined total of $899.16.
